title: Look what we did: why a founder says "we" and sees a company as a tree, not a seed
summary: Jason Cohen reflects on being credited with creating WP Engine and reframes the founder as only the seed of a tree that hundreds of people sustain. He argues a company's purpose lies in the journey and in what each person gains from their time there, not in the founder's glory.

principles.text: The founder is the seed, not the tree. Credit the hundreds of people who build the company every day.
principles.quote: "WP Engine is an oak tree," I explain. "I was the seed. The tree wouldn't exist without the seed, so the seed *was* important, and holds a special and permanent place in the history of the tree. But nothing you see today is the seed.

principles.text: Most of what keeps a company alive is invisible: security upgrades, finance, quality practice. All of it is vital.
principles.quote: things you cannot are the 3am security upgrade and the start of a long-term new product category and brand strategy and collecting accounts receivable and quarterly financial reporting

principles.text: Employees will eventually leave, so make the company a place they look back on as time well spent.
principles.quote: It's up to all of us to make sure each person will look back on their time at WP Engine as well-spent.

principles.text: Judge a company by what it does for people's lives: growth, careers, firsts, and impact on customers and the next generation.
principles.quote: Did they grow as a person, as well as professionally? Did they have an impact on others' lives, where they helped the next generation thrive as they have?

principles.text: A company, like a life, finds its purpose in the journey, not the end.
